intro.data: A functor must also lift the do-nothing step to a do-nothing step. The tray holds two batch lifts plus the Batch Cleaner: one lift truly holds the whole batch unchanged (the lift of the plain identity), the other tampers with it — and then the Batch Cleaner jams on records it didn't expect. Bring the faithful lift and the Batch Cleaner onto the board and wire them, leaving the tamperer in the tray.
intro.alchemy: A functor must lift the do-nothing step to a do-nothing step. The tray holds two crate lifts plus the Crate Smelter: one holds the whole crate unchanged, the other taints it — and then the Crate Smelter jams. Bring the faithful lift and the Crate Smelter onto the board and wire them, leaving the tainter in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: A functor must lift the do-nothing step to a do-nothing step. The tray holds two flock lifts plus the Flock Kindler: one holds the whole flock unchanged, the other warps it — and then the Flock Kindler jams. Bring the faithful lift and the Flock Kindler onto the board and wire them, leaving the warper in the tray.
intro.abstract: F(x) means the value x lifted into the batch world (the box holding x), and a functor's lift does f to each item inside — so it must preserve identity: F(id) = id, sending F(5) ↦ F(5) unchanged. The tray holds the faithful lifted identity, a tamperer (F(5) ↦ F(7), so F(f) then jams), and F(f) (F(5) ↦ F(20)); bring the faithful lift and F(f) onto the board and wire them, leaving the tamperer behind.

goal.data: Bring the faithful lift and the Batch Cleaner from the tray and wire them so the batch reaches the clean batch, leaving the tamperer in the tray.
goal.alchemy: Bring the faithful lift and the Crate Smelter from the tray and wire them so the crate reaches the ingots, leaving the tainter in the tray.
goal.spellcraft: Bring the faithful lift and the Flock Kindler from the tray and wire them so the flock reaches the flames, leaving the warper in the tray.
goal.abstract: Bring the lifted identity and F(f) from the tray and wire them to reach F(B), leaving the tamperer behind.

afterSuccess.data: The faithful lift held the batch unchanged, so the Batch Cleaner saw exactly the records it expected. The tampering look-alike was the same type but altered the batch and jammed the next step. A functor must lift identity to identity: F(id_A) = id_F(A).
afterSuccess.alchemy: The faithful lift held the crate unchanged. The tainting look-alike jammed the next step. A functor must lift identity to identity: F(id_A) = id_F(A).
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The faithful lift held the flock unchanged. The warping look-alike jammed the next step. A functor must lift identity to identity: F(id_A) = id_F(A).
afterSuccess.abstract: The genuine functor lifts identity to identity; the look-alike does not. F(id_A) = id_F(A).

reveal.summary: A functor preserves identities and composition: F(id_A) = id_F(A) and F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f). These two laws are exactly what make a lift a functor.
reveal.moreFormal: A bare assignment of objects and morphisms is a functor only if it respects identities and composition. List, Optional, and Batch all do; a tampering 'lift' does not.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: map(id) === id and map(g ∘ f) === map(g) ∘ map(f) — the Functor laws.
